maya: Heads up — I'm seeing a regression in streaming token latency after yesterday's batching heuristic tweak. Dashboard (per-route) shows chat.generate-v2-prod p95 jump from ~24ms -> ~48ms for token emit. Client-side stalls observed, server chunk cadence looks misaligned. snapshot of rollup metrics below:

maya: ```
route: chat.generate-v2-prod
p50_token_latency_ms: 18
p95_token_latency_ms: 48
client_emit_ms: 12
server_process_ms: 28
server_send_ms: 6
network_ms: 2
total_ms: 48
baseline_p95_ms: 24
kv_evictions_per_min: 42 (baseline 6)
kernel_fallback_rate: 7% (baseline 0.5%)
```

jason: Do you have a trace id or span so I can pull flamegraphs? Any obvious KV cache churn or eviction spikes in the timeline?

maya: Trace id: trace-0x9a3f. Key points around 2026-03-12T14:52:30 UTC show rapid KV evictions and a sudden kernel_selector fallback. Logs: ```
[14:52:29.874] kvcache::evict shard=3 evicted=68
[14:52:29.875] kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_large_gemm reason=throughput_est
[14:52:29.876] kernel_fallback: from=int8 to=fp16 cause=kv_miss_penalty
[14:52:29.877] stream: chunk_emitted seq=120 client_ack_delay_ms=22
[14:52:29.879] stream: chunk_sent seq=120 server_send_delay_ms=14
```

rachel: FYI PR #2345 changed batching heuristic: max_batch_wait_ms from 8 -> 20. That could increase accumulation and increase first-token latency and chunk gaps. Might explain the server-side token processing jump.

eli: Two related things here: 1) client <-> server timing mismatch (client_ack_delay_ms=22 suggests client side too slow or clock skew), and 2) kernel_selector choosing larger GEMMs increases first-token latency. We should add per-chunk timestamps (client_send_ts, server_recv_ts, server_send_ts) to the token-level telemetry so we can distinguish network vs scheduling vs kernel latency precisely.

eli: Proposed minimal instrumentation snippet to add to runtime agent: ```
// on receive
chunk.client_send_ts = headers["x-client-send-ts"] || now_ms();
chunk.server_recv_ts = now_ms();
process_chunk(chunk) { ... }
chunk.server_send_ts = now_ms();
emit_metric("token.latency.components", {
  client_to_server: chunk.server_recv_ts - chunk.client_send_ts,
  server_processing: chunk.server_send_ts - chunk.server_recv_ts,
  server_send: server_network_send_delay
});
```

jason: Also saw kernel_selector heuristics were tweaked in the same deployment. It now prefers the larger batched GEMM with lower amortized cost but higher cold-start first-token cost. Add a flag to prefer low-latency first-token for interactive routes.

rachel: Can we add the following per-route KPIs to the dashboard ASAP: p50/p95 token latency, chunk_gap_histogram, kv_evictions_per_min, kernel_fallback_rate, first_token_cost_ms? That will make regressions obvious.

maya: I'm pushing a staging build with three changes: rollback batching change (max_batch_wait_ms -> 8), add client ts headers instrumentation, and enable prefer_low_latency_first_token for chat.generate-v2-prod. Rolling to staging now. Will run a synthetic stream load and compare. :eyes:

build-bot: deploy triggered: staging/build-2026.3.12-88 by maya

jason: When you run the synthetic test, include a client that simulates 10ms vs 25ms ack delays so we can see interaction between client pacing and server batching. If we see p95 improvements only for the 10ms clients, it's a batching pacing mismatch.

eli: If rollback fixes it, we should prepare a hotfix to prod plus an alert: token_p95_delta > 15ms for any production route triggers a runbook. Also add an anomaly alert on kv_evictions_per_min doubling in a 1m window.

maya: Running test now, initial quick numbers after rollback + instrumentation on staging (10k requests):```
route: chat.generate-v2-prod (staging)
p95_token_latency_ms: 26
kv_evictions_per_min: 8
kernel_fallback_rate: 0.8%
chunk_gap_p95_ms: 9
```

maya: Early signal looks promising vs prod. I'll keep this thread updated after the 20m A/B run completes. Planning a hotfix if the trend holds. :rocket:
